mission.core_purpose: To make the rich heritage of the Jain community accessible to a global audience by digitizing, contextualizing, and publicizing rare manuscript collections.
key_objectives: Provide authoritative, peer-reviewed commentary on complex theological materials.
Foster cross-cultural education and religious literacy.

funding_and_support.additional_support: Private donations from the global Jain diaspora

manuscript_digitization.description: High-resolution digital preservation of rare palm-leaf and paper manuscripts.

educational_resources: Expert-written articles exploring Jain philosophy, history, and art.
Interactive multi-media learning modules for schools.
Curated image galleries displaying intricate manuscript illustrations.

historical_milestones.description: The Institute of Jainology identifies the need to unite fragmented, highly restricted Jain manuscript collections hidden across major UK national institutions.
Establishment of formal collaboration agreements with major national libraries and museums to unlock archival vaults for digitization.
Public rollout of the JAINpedia web portal, backed by academic editorial boards to ensure historical and theological accuracy.

institutional_significance.cultural_preservation: Acts as a bridge between ancient monastic repositories and modern digital humanities.
institutional_significance.educational_impact: Integrates Jain history directly into mainstream theological and historical curricula through vetted digital modules.
